rag_usage_hints: For deterministic unit-test success responses, prefer retrofit2.Response.success(body) when only the body matters.
Use Response.success(code, body) only with a successful HTTP status code.
Use Response.error(code, responseBody) for deterministic HTTP error responses; the code must be 400 or greater.
Response.body() may be null. Generated tests should respect the production method's null-body behavior.
Response.errorBody() is populated for error responses; Response.body() is the success body.
Do not mock retrofit2.Response when a real Response.success(...) or Response.error(...) fixture can be constructed with verified APIs.
Response.error(...) requires okhttp3.ResponseBody. Ensure the project has a version-compatible verified ResponseBody construction API before generating the fixture.
Retrofit service methods may be suspend functions and can return a body type directly or Response<T>; inspect the verified service declaration before choosing a test fixture shape.
